# Model and source

* Citation: `r readModelDb("Dimelow_2023_belimumab")()$meta$reference`
* Description: `r readModelDb("Dimelow_2023_belimumab")()$meta$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.12919>

Belimumab neutralises B-lymphocyte stimulator (BLyS) and depletes the B cells
that depend on it for survival, but circulating memory B cells rise when
treatment starts. Dimelow 2023 pooled memory B-cell counts from 1880
belimumab-treated patients in seven trials and compared two mechanisms. The
stimulatory model (Model A, Table 1) fitted better than the inhibitory one
(Model B), and the final Model D adds baseline BLyS and baseline anti-dsDNA
covariates. Model D was refit in Stan/Torsten, and its posterior medians
(Table 2) are the values packaged here.

The memory B-cell model is Dimelow 2023 Figure 2a:

```
dM/dt = KM * MEMBL * ST(C) * P - KM * M,      M(0) = MEMBL
dP/dt = KP - KP * STP(C) * P,                  P(0) = 1
ST(C)  = 1 + Emax  * C / (EC50 + C)
STP(C) = 1 + EmaxP * C / (EC50 + C)
KP = theta * KM
```

`M` is the circulating memory B-cell concentration (cells/uL, the observed
quantity) and `P` is an unobserved pool of memory B cells in lymphoid organs
and/or inflamed tissues, relative to its baseline. Belimumab first increases
transit from `P` into the circulation (`ST`) and slowly depletes `P` (`STP`),
so circulating cells rise over 4-8 weeks and then return towards baseline.

Individual belimumab PK was not observed in this analysis. Each patient's
profile was derived from the two-compartment population PK model for the
route they received, using population typical values with the body weight
and BMI effects (Dimelow 2023 Table S1). The IV set is from Struemper 2013
and the SC set from Struemper 2018. Both are carried in this one model file
and selected with `ROUTE_IV` (1 = IV, dose into `central`; 0 = SC, dose into
`depot`).

In the packaged model `M` is the `bcell` state, `P` is `bcell_periph`,
`KM` is `kout`, `KP` is `kout_bcell_periph`, `Emax` / `EmaxP` are `emax` /
`emax_bcell_periph`, and `MEMBL` is `rbase`.

# Population

The analysis dataset held 2753 patients with SLE (Dimelow 2023 Figure S1):
1880 received belimumab and 873 placebo. Placebo patients showed no
memory B-cell response and were not used in the fit. The belimumab patients
were 1216 adults on IV, 611 adults on SC and 53 children aged 5-17 years on
IV (PLUTO). The seven studies were LBSL02, BEL112232, BEL115471 (EMBRACE, Black
African ancestry), BEL112341 (BLISS-SC), BEL114055 (PLUTO, pediatric),
BEL113750 (Northeast Asia) and BEL110751 (BLISS-76) (Figure 1).

Pooled baseline characteristics (Table S2, N = 2753) were: median age 39
years (range 6-77), weight 68.5 kg (IQR 57.7-83.0), BMI 25.68 kg/m^2 (IQR
22.08-30.92), BLyS 1.13 ng/mL (IQR 0.70-1.77), anti-dsDNA 79 IU/mL (IQR
29-201; range 1-15001) and memory B cells 15 cells/uL (IQR 7-30). Memory B cells
were total CD19+ CD20+ CD27+ cells by flow cytometry.

```{r population}
str(readModelDb("Dimelow_2023_belimumab")()$population)
```

# Virtual cohort

Covariates are drawn from log-normal distributions matched to the Table S2
medians and interquartile ranges (sdlog = log(Q3/Q1) / 1.349), truncated to
the reported ranges. Each regimen arm has 200 adults.

```{r cohort}
mod <- readModelDb("Dimelow_2023_belimumab")
n_arm <- 200
draw_lnorm <- function(n, med, q1, q3, lo, hi) {
  x <- exp(rnorm(n, log(med), log(q3 / q1) / 1.349))
  pmin(pmax(x, lo), hi)
}
set.seed(2023)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2023)
arms <- c("1 mg/kg IV", "10 mg/kg IV", "200 mg SC")
cohort <- data.frame(
  id = seq_len(3 * n_arm),
  treatment = rep(arms, each = n_arm),
  WT = draw_lnorm(3 * n_arm, 68.5, 57.7, 83.0, 40, 169.5),
  BMI = draw_lnorm(3 * n_arm, 25.68, 22.08, 30.92, 14.32, 65.62),
  SBLYS = draw_lnorm(3 * n_arm, 1.13, 0.70, 1.77, 0.01, 51),
  ANTIDSDNA_BL = draw_lnorm(3 * n_arm, 79, 29, 201, 1, 15001)
) |>
  mutate(ROUTE_IV = as.integer(treatment != "200 mg SC"))
```

```{r events}
obs_days <- sort(unique(c(0:14, seq(0, 364, by = 7))))
iv_days <- c(0, 14, seq(28, 364, by = 28))
sc_days <- seq(0, 357, by = 7)

doses <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(cohort)), function(i) {
  s <- cohort[i, ]
  if (s$treatment == "200 mg SC") {
    data.frame(id = s$id, time = sc_days, amt = 200, cmt = "depot")
  } else {
    mgkg <- if (s$treatment == "1 mg/kg IV") 1 else 10
    data.frame(id = s$id, time = iv_days, amt = mgkg * s$WT, cmt = "central")
  }
})) |>
  mutate(evid = 1L)
obs <- tidyr::crossing(id = cohort$id, time = obs_days) |>
  mutate(amt = NA_real_, cmt = "bcell", evid = 0L)
events <- bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
  left_join(cohort, by = "id") |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod, events = events,
  keep = c("treatment", "WT", "SBLYS", "ANTIDSDNA_BL")
) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  group_by(id) |>
  mutate(fc = bcell / bcell[time == 0], fc_periph = bcell_periph) |>
  ungroup()
```

# Belimumab PK layer

The PK layer is a set of fixed literature typical values, so it is checked
against closed-form steady-state identities rather than refitted. For a
linear model the steady-state average concentration is
`Cav = F * Dose / (CL * tau)`. The Discussion of Dimelow 2023 quotes an average
steady-state concentration of about 100 ug/mL for both approved regimens, and
about 25 ug/mL after the first 200 mg SC dose.

```{r pk-nca}
# Typical (median-covariate) subject per approved regimen, sampled densely
# over the dosing interval starting at week 48 (finely just after the dose,
# where the IV bolus decline is steepest).
typ <- data.frame(
  id = 1:2, treatment = c("10 mg/kg IV", "200 mg SC"),
  WT = 68.5, BMI = 25.68, SBLYS = 1.13, ANTIDSDNA_BL = 79,
  ROUTE_IV = c(1L, 0L)
)
t_start <- 336
typ_dose <- bind_rows(
  data.frame(id = 1L, time = iv_days, amt = 10 * 68.5, cmt = "central"),
  data.frame(id = 2L, time = sc_days, amt = 200, cmt = "depot")
) |>
  mutate(evid = 1L) |>
  # No dose at the interval end, so the closing sample is the trough rather
  # than the next post-dose peak.
  filter(time <= t_start)
typ_obs <- tidyr::crossing(
  id = 1:2,
  time = sort(unique(c(0, seq(t_start, t_start + 2, by = 0.02), seq(t_start, t_start + 28, by = 0.25))))
) |>
  mutate(amt = NA_real_, cmt = "central", evid = 0L)
typ_ev <- bind_rows(typ_dose, typ_obs) |>
  left_join(typ, by = "id") |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
# omega = NA, sigma = NA: typical values (all etas and residuals zero).
typ_sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = typ_ev, omega = NA, sigma = NA,
                           keep = "treatment") |>
  as.data.frame()

conc <- typ_sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, treatment, time, Cc)
tau <- c("10 mg/kg IV" = 28, "200 mg SC" = 7)
intervals <- data.frame(
  treatment = names(tau), start = t_start, end = t_start + tau,
  cav = TRUE, cmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time | treatment + id, concu = "ug/mL", timeu = "day"),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(typ_dose |> left_join(typ[, c("id", "treatment")], by = "id"),
                   amt ~ time | treatment + id, doseu = "mg"),
  intervals = intervals
))
nca_tbl <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result)

cl_iv <- 0.215 * (68.5 / 66.3)^0.506
cl_sc <- 0.204 * (68.5 / 67)^0.75
closed_form <- data.frame(
  treatment = c("10 mg/kg IV", "200 mg SC"),
  cav = c(685 / (cl_iv * 28), 0.742 * 200 / (cl_sc * 7))
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_tbl, reference = closed_form, by = "treatment",
  params = "cav", units = c(cav = "ug/mL"), tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Steady-state average belimumab concentration, simulated (PKNCA) vs F * Dose / (CL * tau).")

cav_sim <- nca_tbl |> filter(PPTESTCD == "cav") |> arrange(treatment)
stopifnot(
  # Same drawn parameters on both sides: only integration and trapezoid error.
  all(abs(cav_sim$PPORRES / closed_form$cav - 1) < 0.01),
  # Discussion: average steady-state concentration "~100 ug/ml".
  all(abs(cav_sim$PPORRES / 100 - 1) < 0.2)
)
```

```{r first-dose}
first_sc <- sim |>
  filter(treatment == "200 mg SC", time > 0, time <= 7) |>
  group_by(id) |>
  summarise(cmax1 = max(Cc))
median(first_sc$cmax1)
# Discussion: after the first SC dose serum concentrations reach ~25 ug/ml.
stopifnot(abs(median(first_sc$cmax1) / 25 - 1) < 0.25)
```

# Covariate effects (Figure 3b)

Figure 3b plots, for each retained covariate-parameter pair, the ratio of the
parameter at the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles of the covariate to its value at
the median. The 2.5th / 97.5th percentiles themselves are not reported, so
they are back-solved from one ratio each (anti-dsDNA from the Emax points,
BLyS from its single pair). With a power model the same pair of anti-dsDNA
percentiles must then reproduce the EmaxP and KM ratios, which tests the
printed exponents.

```{r fig3b}
theta <- c(emax = 0.0535, emax_p = 0.192, km_dsdna = -0.0756, km_blys = -0.125)
# Points digitised from Figure 3b by the maintainers (2.5th, 97.5th).
fig3b <- data.frame(
  pair = c("anti-dsDNA on Emax", "anti-dsDNA on EmaxP", "anti-dsDNA on KM", "BLyS on KM"),
  p025 = c(0.84, 0.54, 1.28, 1.44),
  p975 = c(1.19, 1.83, 0.79, 0.84)
)
dsdna_pct <- 79 * c(fig3b$p025[1], fig3b$p975[1])^(1 / theta[["emax"]])
blys_pct <- 1.13 * c(fig3b$p025[4], fig3b$p975[4])^(1 / theta[["km_blys"]])
round(c(dsdna_pct, blys_pct), 3)

model_ratio <- rbind(
  (dsdna_pct / 79)^theta[["emax"]],
  (dsdna_pct / 79)^theta[["emax_p"]],
  (dsdna_pct / 79)^theta[["km_dsdna"]],
  (blys_pct / 1.13)^theta[["km_blys"]]
)
fig3b$model_p025 <- round(model_ratio[, 1], 3)
fig3b$model_p975 <- round(model_ratio[, 2], 3)
fig3b |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Covariate on parameter" = pair,
    "Figure 3b, 2.5th" = p025, "Figure 3b, 97.5th" = p975,
    "Model, 2.5th" = model_p025, "Model, 97.5th" = model_p975
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Replicates the point estimates of Figure 3b of Dimelow 2023.")

# The EmaxP and KM rows are predictions, not inputs: a mis-transcribed
# exponent moves them by more than the +/-0.06 digitisation error.
stopifnot(
  all(abs(fig3b$model_p025[2:3] - fig3b$p025[2:3]) < 0.06),
  all(abs(fig3b$model_p975[2:3] - fig3b$p975[2:3]) < 0.06)
)
```

The back-solved anti-dsDNA percentiles (about 3 and 2000 IU/mL) are plausible
for a cohort whose range is 1-15001 IU/mL (Table S2), and the BLyS
percentiles (about 0.06 and 4.6 ng/mL) for a range of 0.01-51 ng/mL.

# Memory B-cell response (Figure 4)

```{r fig4, fig.height = 4}
summ <- sim |>
  select(treatment, time, Circulation = fc, Periphery = fc_periph) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Circulation, Periphery), names_to = "panel", values_to = "fc") |>
  group_by(treatment, panel, time) |>
  summarise(
    p05 = quantile(fc, 0.05), p25 = quantile(fc, 0.25), med = median(fc),
    p75 = quantile(fc, 0.75), p95 = quantile(fc, 0.95), .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(filter(summ, treatment == "10 mg/kg IV"), aes(time / 7)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), fill = "grey85") +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p25, ymax = p75), fill = "grey55") +
  geom_line(aes(y = med)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~panel, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Time (weeks)", y = "Memory B cells (fold change from baseline)",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 4 of Dimelow 2023: 10 mg/kg IV. Median, IQR and 90% prediction interval.")
```

```{r fig5a, fig.height = 4}
summ_circ <- sim |>

            .groups = "drop")
ggplot(summ_circ, aes(time / 7)) +

```

# Comparison with the reported response

Reference values are from the Discussion (200 mg SC weekly: median
fold-change 1.67 at week 1 and 2.21 at week 4) and, read off the figures by
the maintainers, the 10 mg/kg IV medians of Figure 4.

```{r compare}
pick <- function(trt, pan, day) {
  v <- summ$med[summ$treatment == trt & summ$panel == pan & summ$time == day]
  if (length(v) != 1L) stop("no unique row for ", trt, " / ", pan, " / day ", day)
  v
}
ref <- data.frame(
  quantity = c(
    "200 mg SC, circulating, week 1", "200 mg SC, circulating, week 4",
    "10 mg/kg IV, circulating, week 8", "10 mg/kg IV, circulating, week 52",
    "10 mg/kg IV, periphery, week 24", "10 mg/kg IV, periphery, week 52"
  ),
  source = c("Discussion", "Discussion", "Figure 4 (digitised)", "Figure 4 (digitised)",
             "Figure 4 (digitised)", "Figure 4 (digitised)"),
  # Figure 4 medians digitised on its log axes: circulation 2.27 (week 8) and
  # 1.27 (week 52); periphery 0.44 (week 24) and 0.31 (week 52).
  reported = c(1.67, 2.21, 2.27, 1.27, 0.44, 0.31),
  deviation = c(FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE, TRUE),
  simulated = c(
    pick("200 mg SC", "Circulation", 7), pick("200 mg SC", "Circulation", 28),
    pick("10 mg/kg IV", "Circulation", 56), pick("10 mg/kg IV", "Circulation", 364),
    pick("10 mg/kg IV", "Periphery", 168), pick("10 mg/kg IV", "Periphery", 364)
  )
) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = round(100 * (simulated / reported - 1), 1),
         simulated = round(simulated, 2))
ref |>
  dplyr::rename("Median fold change" = quantity, Source = source,
                Reported = reported, Simulated = simulated, "% diff" = pct_diff,
                "Known deviation" = deviation) |>
  knitr::kable()

# Centre of the distribution only (no extremes). A mis-transcribed Emax, KM or
# ratio moves these medians by far more than 25%. The periphery rows are a
# known deviation (discussed below) and are reported but not gated.
stopifnot(all(abs(ref$pct_diff[!ref$deviation]) < 25))
```

The simulated circulating medians are within about 10% of the reported ones,
mostly below them. The unobserved peripheral pool is depleted more slowly
than in Figure 4: its median is about 35% above the figure at weeks 24 and 52.
The typical-value subject is closer, with the peripheral pool at 0.52 at
week 26 and 0.35 at week 52 for 10 mg/kg IV. The typical-value subject (median covariates, all etas zero) reaches a
fold-change of about 2.5 at week 4, but the median across subjects is lower
because of the large between-patient variability on KM (log-scale SD 1.16).
Dimelow 2023 estimated a full correlation matrix for the four random effects
(LKJ prior) but did not report it, so the etas here are independent. That is
the most likely cause of the gap. It also means this model cannot reproduce
Figure 5b, where patients with low baseline memory B cells have larger fold
changes. With independent etas the fold change does not depend on MEMBL at
all, so that dependence must come from a correlation between MEMBL and Emax
and/or KM.

```{r baseline-independence}
# Fold change vs baseline memory B cells (Figure 5b stratification): with
# independent etas the quartile medians are flat, unlike Figure 5b.
sim |>
  filter(treatment == "200 mg SC", time == 28) |>
  mutate(baseline_quartile = cut(rbase, c(0, 7, 15, 30, Inf),
                                 labels = c("<=7", "7-15", "15-30", ">30"))) |>
  group_by(baseline_quartile) |>
  summarise(n = n(), median_fc_week4 = round(median(fc), 2)) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Random-effect correlations not reported.** Table 2 gives the log-scale
  SD of each random effect (posterior median), and the text says the
  correlation matrix had an LKJ(2) prior, but the posterior correlations are
  not published. The four etas are entered as independent with variance =
  SD^2. The consequences are discussed above. The circulating median fold change
  is up to about 10% low. The median peripheral pool is about 35% above Figure 4
  and is excluded from the validation gate. The baseline dependence in Figure 5b
  is not reproduced.
* **Posterior medians as point estimates.** The packaged values are the Stan
  posterior medians of Table 2. Population predictions in the paper integrate
  over the posterior, so they are not exactly reproducible from point
  estimates.
* **PK typical values only.** Following the paper, the PK layer has no
  between-subject variability beyond body weight and BMI, and all PK values
  are fixed. The SC V2 weight effect is printed as `(WT/67)` in Table S1 and
  is entered with exponent 1. The source SC popPK paper (Struemper 2018, packaged as
  `Struemper_2017_belimumab`) fixed it at 0.8, and that model also has
  albumin and IgG effects on CL that Dimelow 2023 does not list. This
  model follows Table S1. Pediatric patients used the adult IV parameters,
  as in the paper.
* **Covariate distributions.** The virtual cohort draws weight, BMI, BLyS and
  anti-dsDNA independently from log-normal distributions matched to Table S2
  (pooled belimumab + placebo); correlations between covariates are ignored.
  The cohort is adult-only.
* **Figure readings.** The Figure 3b points and the Figure 4 medians in the
  comparison table were read off the published figures by the maintainers.
* **Covariates screened but not retained.** Body weight, BMI, age, baseline
  C3, C4 and SELENA-SLEDAI were screened against the week-8 simulated
  response (Table S3) and not retained for the memory B-cell parameters.
  Weight and BMI enter only through the PK.
